results.executiveVerdict: The marketing hero section has several issues with visual hierarchy and UX that need attention to improve user experience and accessibility.

findings.issue: In primary reading path, the primary reading path is not strong enough to make priority immediately clear.
findings.evidence: the leading heading is "Operate every launch from one connected workspace"; the strongest visible action appears to be "Explore workflow"; the hero visual area, heading, and CTA/action group share the opening scan path.
findings.impact: Users may need to inspect more of the screen before understanding the main message, priority action, or intended order of attention.
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the hierarchy from primary message to supporting detail to action, and reduce competing emphasis around secondary content.

findings.issue: In action path, the intended next action is not communicated with enough certainty.
findings.evidence: Visible primary and secondary actions include "Start review", "Explore workflow"; their size, placement, and visual weight are close enough to increase decision effort.
findings.impact: When users cannot quickly distinguish the preferred action from supporting actions, decision effort increases and completion confidence drops.
findings.recommendation: Make the primary action visually dominant, connect it more clearly to the headline or task context, and reduce secondary action emphasis.

findings.issue: In readable content, some content may be visually harder to read or activate than it should be.
findings.evidence: 1 readability or contrast risk signal(s); 1 accessibility-visible finding(s) were generated.
findings.impact: Soft text, small targets, or unclear visual states can reduce confidence for users with low vision, motor needs, glare, or cognitive fatigue.
findings.recommendation: Increase text clarity, preserve comfortable hit areas, and ensure important states are communicated with more than colour alone.

findings.issue: In text contrast, some text appears visually soft against its background.
findings.evidence: "Plan releases, review design quality, align stakeholders, track risks, and prepare teams." has an estimated contrast ratio of 3.89.
findings.impact: Users with low vision, glare-heavy viewing conditions, or cognitive fatigue may need more effort to read this content.
findings.recommendation: Increase the foreground/background separation for this text, especially if it carries navigation, instructions, status, or decision-critical content.

results.executiveVerdict: Visual hierarchy and enterprise polish issues identified in Zeplin Artboard review

findings.issue: In central artboard hierarchy, the primary reading path is not strong enough to make priority immediately clear.
findings.evidence: the leading heading is "Vakgebieden"; the strongest visible action appears to be "Find jobs"; the hero visual area, heading, and CTA/action group share the opening scan path; the central design area contains the main artboard hierarchy rather than editor chrome.
findings.impact: Users may need to inspect more of the screen before understanding the main message, priority action, or intended order of attention.
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the hierarchy from primary message to supporting detail to action, and reduce competing emphasis around secondary content.

findings.issue: In testimonial block, the testimonial treatment may compete with the credibility of the quote.
findings.evidence: Within the central artboard, the testimonial/quote area is visually prominent enough to affect polish and trust.
findings.impact: If decorative quote treatment competes with the actual testimonial text or attribution, the section can feel less credible and less editorially mature.
findings.recommendation: Make the quote text and attribution the clearest elements, then reduce any decorative treatment that competes with readability.

results.executiveVerdict: Design system inconsistencies and visual hierarchy weaknesses identified in Figma frame cards and central artboard hierarchy.

findings.issue: In figma frame cards, repeated components do not feel governed by one consistent system.
findings.evidence: 3 frame card component(s); 2 rounded-corner treatments; 1 elevation/shadow treatments.
findings.impact: Visual drift across repeated components makes the product feel less mature and can make similar controls appear to behave differently.
findings.recommendation: Standardise repeated component states, radius, elevation, spacing, and icon treatment through a smaller set of reusable patterns.

findings.issue: In central artboard hierarchy, the primary reading path is not strong enough to make priority immediately clear.
findings.evidence: the leading heading is "Bring design review into the release workflow"; the central design area contains the main artboard hierarchy rather than editor chrome.
findings.impact: Users may need to inspect more of the screen before understanding the main message, priority action, or intended order of attention.
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the hierarchy from primary message to supporting detail to action, and reduce competing emphasis around secondary content.
